skill.name: pylabrobot
skill.description: PyLabRobot guidance for designing, simulating, and documenting laboratory automation protocols. It covers liquid handlers, resources, hardware backends, analytical devices, material handling, and visualization workflows.
skill.summary: Build and review PyLabRobot laboratory automation protocols.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Laboratory automation code can be difficult to structure across devices and labware. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create PyLabRobot protocols with clear resources, backends, simulation, and safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains PyLabRobot setup for liquid handlers, plate readers, pumps, shakers, incubators, and centrifuges.
Shows how to define deck resources, plates, tip racks, troughs, carriers, and saved layouts.
Provides examples for Hamilton STAR, Opentrons OT-2, Tecan EVO, and simulation backends.
Describes volume tracking, tip tracking, liquid classes, and resource state serialization.
Guides protocol validation with ChatterboxBackend and the browser visualizer.
Documents patterns for multi-device workflows that combine pipetting and measurements.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not verified execution against a real instrument.
Hardware compatibility depends on the installed PyLabRobot version and device firmware.
Users must validate protocols in simulation before running physical hardware.
It does not replace laboratory safety review or instrument-specific operating procedures.

use_cases.title: Design a Liquid Transfer Protocol
use_cases.description: Create a PyLabRobot workflow with tip handling, deck resources, and volume tracking before hardware use.

use_cases.title: Prepare Device Integration Notes
use_cases.description: Compare backend setup patterns for Hamilton, Opentrons, simulation, and analytical equipment.

use_cases.title: Review Protocol Readiness
use_cases.description: Check resource definitions, state tracking, cleanup paths, and simulation coverage before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PyLabRobot liquid transfer plan for one source plate, one destination plate, and one tip rack. Include setup, tracking, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Deck Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a deck layout for a Hamilton STAR with two tip racks, a trough, a source plate, and a destination plate. Explain each resource choice.

prompt_templates.title: Simulate Before Hardware
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned PyLabRobot workflow and convert it into a simulation-first process using ChatterboxBackend, tracking, and visualizer checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multiple Devices
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-device PyLabRobot workflow that prepares samples, controls temperature, reads a plate, records measurements, and stops each device safely.

output_examples.input: I need a protocol outline for transferring samples from one 96-well plate to another.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with deck resources, tip pickup, transfer steps, volume tracking, cleanup, and simulation checks.

output_examples.input: I want to connect an Opentrons OT-2 backend and avoid hardcoding production details.
output_examples.output: A configuration checklist that separates robot host settings, deck setup, simulation mode, and hardware validation steps.

output_examples.input: Please review my automation workflow before I run it on hardware.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering resource names, liquid volumes, tip handling, error cleanup, and required simulation results.

best_practices: Start every workflow in simulation and keep hardware execution behind an explicit choice.
Track tips, volumes, deck layouts, and initial states for reproducible protocols.
Use clear resource names and stop every connected device in cleanup paths.
anti_patterns: Running new protocols on physical hardware before simulation and visual inspection.
Hardcoding lab-specific robot hosts in shared examples without configuration guidance.
Ignoring instrument setup, calibration, liquid limits, or laboratory safety procedures.

faq.question: Does this skill run laboratory equipment by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides PyLabRobot guidance and examples. Users decide what code to run in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help with Hamilton STAR protocols?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include setup patterns, deck resources, liquid transfers, and simulation practices for Hamilton STAR workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with Opentrons OT-2?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Opentrons backend examples and reminds users to configure the robot host for their lab.

faq.question: Should I test protocols before hardware use?
faq.answer: Yes. Use simulation, tracking, and visualization before physical execution.

faq.question: Does it include plate reader guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CLARIOstar examples, absorbance, luminescence, fluorescence, temperature setup, and liquid handler integration.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for lab safety review?
faq.answer: No. Human review, equipment procedures, and laboratory safety controls remain required.
